hard_decision_rules: Canonical identities are preserved unless a real alias/duplicate is proven.
One primary SEO owner per intent.
Application/subdiscipline hubs may exist without duplicating their umbrella owner's generic intents.
Provider raw rows do not create article intents and missing exact rows do not erase subject-defined distinct article intents.
No target-tree write before the full 841-entry assessment is complete.

decisions.ownership: Owns generic amateur-radio orientation, licensing, station basics, bands and operating overview. Satellitenfunk, Morsefunk and Funkpeilung keep their specific practice intents. CB-Funk remains legally and structurally separate; SDR remains a separate receiving/experimentation identity.
Owns CB-specific rules, equipment, antennas, operating practice, range and troubleshooting. Amateurfunk generic/licensing intents do not move here.

Owns generic SDR hardware, software operation, antennas for SDR, signal decoding and SDR projects. Specific satellite, radiosonde and amateur-radio operating intents stay with their dedicated identities.

Owns amateur-radio satellite passes, station/equipment, satellite antennas/tracking and satellite QSOs. Amateurfunk remains the generic orientation owner; non-amateur satellite reception stays outside this hub.

Owns broad receive-only satellite orientation and setup where no stronger specialist owner exists. Amateur-radio satellite operation belongs to Satellitenfunk; generic SDR operation belongs to Software Defined Radio; radiosonde tracking remains separate.
Owns radiosonde identification, reception, tracking/prediction, recovery and field practice. Generic SDR hardware/software stays with SDR; generic radio direction finding stays with Funkpeilung.
Owns direction-finding principles, receivers/peilers, direction-finding antennas and ARDF/field practice. Generic amateur-radio orientation stays with Amateurfunk.
Owns learning Morse/CW, keys/keyers, sending technique, CW QSO practice and reception training. Amateurfunk remains the generic radio owner.

Owns generic electronics-hobby orientation, components, soldering, measurement, breadboards and basic circuits. Arduino, Raspberry-Pi-Projekte and Mikrocontroller-Projekte keep platform/project-specific ownership.

Owns generic microcontroller project orientation independent of a specific platform. Arduino and later platform-specific identities own their platform setup, libraries and concrete platform project intents. Owns Arduino boards/IDE, Arduino-specific pins/power, sensors, actuators and Arduino projects/debugging. Generic microcontroller theory belongs to Mikrocontroller-Projekte.
Owns Raspberry-Pi setup, GPIO/hardware, servers/network, automation and Raspberry-Pi projects/operation. Generic electronics and generic microcontroller intents stay with their umbrella owners.

Owns generic robotics orientation, concepts, sensors, actuators, navigation, control and overview. Roboterbau owns hands-on construction; Heimrobotik owns domestic-robot projects; BattleBots-Modellbau owns combat-robot practice.

Owns home-oriented robot platform projects, domestic sensor/navigation use, mechanics and home autonomy/integration. Generic robot construction stays with Roboterbau; generic robotics concepts stay with Robotik.

Owns hands-on robot planning/chassis, drive, electronics/power, sensors/control and programming/test for generic self-built robots. Heimrobotik and BattleBots keep their application-specific intents; Robotik remains the umbrella orientation owner.
Owns combat-robot-specific rules/safety, chassis/protection, drive/electronics, weapon systems, testing/repair and competition preparation. Generic robot construction remains with Roboterbau.
